title: ANDS Studio — Sign in / create a workspace
walkthrough:
You land on a single centered card on an otherwise empty page. At the top is the product mark "ANDS Studio" with a small dot icon, then the heading "Sign in" and one line of small grey text: "Your clients' dossiers are isolated per workspace." Below are two labeled fields, "Email" (placeholder "ra@company.example") and "Password", then a primary button "Sign in →" next to a plain-text button "New client? Create a workspace". Under those sits a smaller link-style button, "Forgot password?". The primary button stays disabled until both fields have something in them, and reads "Working…" while it submits. Pressing Enter in the password field also submits.

If you sign in against an account that has multi-factor authentication enabled, the card reveals an extra "Authenticator code" field (placeholder "6-digit code") with helper text: "This account has multi-factor authentication enabled — enter the current code from your authenticator app." Entering a wrong code returns the message "That code didn't verify — codes rotate every 30 seconds; try the current one."

Clicking "New client? Create a workspace" swaps the same card into signup mode: the heading becomes "Create your workspace", the subtext becomes "One workspace per client company — dossiers, documents and filings stay isolated.", and a "Company / client name" field appears above Email (placeholder "Northbridge Regulatory CRO"). As you type a password, live helper text below the field shows the rule "At least 10 characters, with letters and numbers.", counts down remaining characters if you are short, and flips to "✓ Meets the password rules." when satisfied. The buttons become "Create workspace →" and "Have an account? Sign in". Errors from either mode appear as a red notice box inside the card.

Choosing "Forgot password?" changes the heading to "Reset your password" with the explanation that a one-time code expiring in 15 minutes will be issued. You enter your email and click "Send me a code →". A notice box then states: "Demo environment — no outbound email. Your one-time code is shown on-screen below. In a production deployment this code is emailed to your address and never displayed." The code appears in that box, followed by a "One-time code" field (placeholder "8-digit code") and a "New password" field. "Set new password →" completes it and returns you to sign-in with the notice "Password updated — sign in with your new password." A "Back to sign in" button is always available.

After signing in or creating a workspace, you are routed to the dossier manager: a top bar with "ANDS Studio", chips for "Help", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence" and "Guided journey →", plus a user chip showing your email and workspace name with a "Sign out" button. The workspace name comes from the server account record. The page heading is "Your product dossiers". The email-and-workspace part of the user chip is itself a link to an "Account & security" page.

That page opens with the heading "Account & security" and four cards. "Who you are here" lists your email ("Signed in as"), your workspace ("from the account record — every dossier, document and filing here is isolated to this workspace"), and your role. "Multi-factor authentication" offers a "Set up authenticator app →" button; enrolling shows Step 1 — a secret code plus a "Copy setup link" button for the otpauth URI — and Step 2 — a "6-digit code" field with a "Turn on MFA →" button and the note "Nothing is enforced until this code verifies — if you stop here, sign-in stays password-only." "Password & sessions" lists three facts: passwords are at least 10 characters with letters and numbers, stored only as salted hashes; changing a password is done by signing out and using "Forgot password?" with a 15-minute one-time code that signs out every other session; sessions last 12 hours and live in an HttpOnly cookie that page scripts can never read. "Deployment & data residency" states that ANDS Studio is self-hosted with every service and database inside your own environment (nothing leaving it except the packages you deliberately transmit to Health Canada), that cross-workspace reads are refused at the API and not just hidden in the UI, that single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) is not yet available, and that every state change lands on an append-only audit event stream.
